verdict.rationale: YYLO is documented as a command-line orchestrator for coding agents. It dispatches a task to a subagent such as Claude, runs it in an isolated task worktree, can repeat iterations until no open kanban work remains, and queues the committed candidate for merge, so the end-to-end implementation loop is covered. Nothing shows the agent writing tests: the docs say tests are separate project checks outside merge, which concerns running suites, not authoring them. Missing for 10: evidence that the agent writes tests as part of a feature, a documented feature-to-tests workflow, and independent or hands-on corroboration of end-to-end feature delivery.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have an agent implement a requested feature end-to-end, including writing tests

citations.quote: YYLO is a command-line orchestrator for coding agents, repeatable workflows, and receipt-backed repository changes.
yylo init --task "Describe one verifiable outcome" --subagent claude
Start hydrates an exact-base task worktree. Preflight is read-only, finish queues the committed candidate
Repeat bounded YYLO iterations until no open kanban work remains.
